chunks: And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That he prayed two rak'ahs in the Mosque of the Tree, and entered into the state of Ihram, then he went out and was brought Khabis (a type of bread) containing saffron, so he ate from it.

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.خَبِيصٌ: A type of bread or cake made with flour and honey/ghee
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ الشَّجَرَةِ: The Mosque of the Tree, a location in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What did the Imam eat while in the state of Ihram according to this narration?
ai.summary: This narration from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the practical flexibility of the Prophet and Imams regarding sustenance during the state of Ihram, specifically addressing the permissibility of consuming flavored foods like Khabis with saffron. It serves as a key evidentiary basis in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between prohibited acts and permissible consumption of food, reinforcing the principle that Ihram restricts specific rituals rather than general nourishment. The mention of the 'Mosque of the Tree' (Masjid al-Shajara) in Mecca adds historical context to the location of this ritual practice.
